# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` fields; all three optional, omitting preserves current behaviour.
- **Cost gating.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `state.resourceBank.coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `state.resourceBank.reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; options with no cost always included.
- **Presented list stability.** `PendingEventChoice.options` stores the draw-time snapshot populated at choice draw time; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
- **Cost deduction.** Selecting an affordable option deducts cost coins and cost reputation from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effects.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`; both can coexist.
- **Loss checks and logging.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire; activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule matching `state.resourceBank` field determines the pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback when no conditions match.
- **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match fallback; matched successor pushed via `pushChainCard`.
- **Precedence.** `successorResolver` wins when present; otherwise conditional rules run before `successorIds` random draw and legacy `successorId`; a matching rule consumes no RNG draw.
- **AI selection.** The AI considers only options in the presented list; when a pending choice exists it reads the frozen pending snapshot, otherwise the state-filtered list.
- **Cost-aware scoring.** Projected option value subtracts `cost.coins` and `cost.reputation` and adds `extraEffect` before comparing options.
- **AI harnesses.** Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections; legacy binary-choice AI behaviour identical.
- **Static validation.** Reject negative or zero costs; reject conditions with unknown field or op; reject non-numeric value; reject negative extra effect values; reject dangling conditional successors.
- **Schema and shipped content.** Shipped content validates cleanly: all shipped CSVs produce valid storylines; JSON schema accepts the new optional fields; doc-drift test passes.
- **Documentation.** `docs/game/storylines.md` documents the extended `StorylineOption` fields `cost`, `extraEffect`, `conditionalSuccessors` with examples; resolution lifecycle documented.
- **Seam, CSV and roadmap docs.** `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` migration notes updated; `src/README.md` confirms the new semantics are programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`, not CSV-authored; roadmap updated.

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only for the new semantics (producer decision
  Q1=A).** Extend the in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and
  schema. The CSV `options` column now authors arbitrary labels/candidate sets
  (MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144), but it must **not** gain cost, extra-effect, or
  conditional-column authoring in this work; those stay programmatic via
  `registerStorylineOptions`.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- **Full suite gate (delivery gate, not a child feature).** Every child's
  definition of done includes a green full project test suite; the epic is not
  complete until the full suite passes with zero behavioural deltas for
  existing content.

## Existing state (verified against the codebase on this plan revision)

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) has since grown beyond the
  original three-field shape: `{ label, successorId? (deprecated), successorIds?
  (random candidate set), effectPolicy, condition? (draw-time callback),
  successorResolver? (resolution-time callback) }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps
  an ordered option list.
- CSV authoring was generalised by MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144: the `options` column
  decodes to arbitrary labelled options with candidate successor sets
  (`parseStorylineOptionsEncoding`), not just two-way Accept/Reject.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice(event, state)` (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`)
  already freezes a draw-time, condition-filtered snapshot onto
  `PendingEventChoice.options`; `getPendingStorylineOptions(pending, state)`
  reads it (with a recompile fallback), and `resolveEventOption`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) already indexes that snapshot and
  records the option label as the transcript token.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)` applies `effectPolicy` and
  resolves the successor with documented precedence: `successorResolver` →
  `successorIds` (one seeded RNG draw) → legacy `successorId`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) already returns an
  option **index** (not binary accept/reject) and picks the option with the
  lowest pessimistic successor severity, but it calls
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` without state and ignores cost/extra effects.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; the canonical docs are
  `docs/game/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10 roadmap),
  `src/README.md`, and `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md`.
- None of `cost`, `extraEffect`, or declarative `conditionalSuccessors` exists
  anywhere in `src/` today — those are the genuine remaining gaps.

## Desired change

Extend the **current** option model and resolution path (which already has
callback conditions, callbacks resolvers, random candidate sets, and a frozen
draw-time snapshot) so that:

1. Options declare an optional declarative affordability `cost`; the
   draw-time presented list (already snapshotted on `PendingEventChoice.options`)
   additionally filters out unaffordable options.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered declarative
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time.
3. Selection applies the `effectPolicy` effect (unchanged), deducts `cost`,
   applies `extraEffect` independently, and pushes the resolver-precedence
   successor, honouring the declarative rules.
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented snapshot and accounts for
   cost/extra-effect deltas.

## Plan revision note (this planning session)

Three of the eight children created by the previous plan run were written
against a superseded code shape. Revision outcome:

- **Closed as already implemented:** "Update engine turn closing to use
  presented option list" — `resolveEventOption` already indexes the frozen
  `pending.options` snapshot with a recompile fallback and label-based
  transcripts (shipped by F3, `MS-0MV8KQL820077BOS`).
- **Rewritten to the remaining gap:** "Add affordability filtering" now covers
  only cost-based filtering on top of the existing snapshot; "AI
  cost-awareness" now targets the existing index-returning `decideEventChoice`;
  "model extension" and "validator/schema" now extend the current field set;
  "documentation" now targets `docs/game/storylines.md`.
- Dependency order is unchanged; test coverage stays embedded per feature
  (TDD within each child) plus the existing regression/Monte Carlo harness.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Add cost filtering to the existing draw-time
  snapshot path, apply cost + extra effects in `resolveStorylineOption`,
  resolve declarative conditional successors by the documented precedence.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingEventChoice.options` snapshot already
  exists; document that it now carries cost-filtered lists (no new field).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Update cost/extra-effect logging and
  totals in `resolveEventOption` (snapshot indexing is already implemented).
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/extra-effect/condition
  data and conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/game/storylines.md`, `src/README.md`,
  `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — Document the extended option
  model, resolution semantics, and programmatic-only authoring.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-regression-harness.test.ts` — New/extended
  coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/game/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Cost filtering changes the index space.** The draw-time snapshot
  (`PendingEventChoice.options`) already freezes the presented list, so cost
  filtering inherits that stability — but the AI must read the snapshot (not
  recompile) or it will disagree with the UI and transcript. *Mitigation:*
  `decideEventChoice` reads `getPendingStorylineOptions` and is covered by
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` already returns an index, but it
  compiles options without state and ignores cost/extra effects; an option that
  is unaffordable in the snapshot must never be scored or chosen.
  *Mitigation:* score only the presented list and include cost/extra deltas;
  cover with regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Precedence ambiguity.** Two successor mechanisms now coexist (callback
  resolver, random candidate set) plus the new declarative rules.
  *Mitigation:* precedence is documented in code and tests (callback >
  declarative rules > random candidates > single successor).
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Callback conditions/resolvers and CSV label authoring have
  already shipped elsewhere (`MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`, `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`); this
  work adds only the declarative cost/extra-effect/conditional-successor fields.
  Per-option animation and CSV cost columns remain out of scope.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
    *Note (plan revision 2026-10-19): the CSV `options` column was later
    generalised to arbitrary labels/candidate sets by `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`;
    the intent of Q1=A still holds — the new cost/extra-effect/conditional
    semantics stay programmatic and add no CSV columns.*
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

- **Q4 — Plan revision against the current codebase (this session).**
  Three of the eight children were drafted against a superseded model. Answer
  (plan skill, evidence-based): close the already-implemented engine child and
  rewrite the rest to the remaining gaps; no new producer decision needed for
  *what* to build, because Q1–Q3 still hold. Sources: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`,
  `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`, `MS-0MV8KQL820077BOS`.

### Assumptions

- **Resolution order.** The `effectPolicy` effect is applied first (preserving
  today's behaviour exactly), then `cost` is deducted, then `extraEffect` is
  applied; the returned `coinChange`/`repChange` deltas cover all three.
- **Successor precedence.** `successorResolver` callback (existing escape
  hatch) > declarative `conditionalSuccessors` (first match wins) >
  `successorIds` random candidate draw > legacy `successorId`. A matching
  conditional rule consumes no RNG draw.
- **Affordability boundary.** An option is affordable when
  `cost.coins <= state.resourceBank.coins` and
  `cost.reputation <= state.resourceBank.reputation` (equality is affordable);
  unspecified cost components are unconstrained.
- **Draw-time filtering order.** The existing `condition` callback filter runs
  first, then the new cost filter — an option must pass both to be presented.

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUO8B93V002CL06** – Help panel content drifts from PRD milestone 5 (7 sections, >8 lines) (in-progress)
- **MS-0MUOSII720060IZQ** – Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw) (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** – Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, actions, actually (+352 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, actions, actually (+276 more)

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/game/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/game/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/game/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   listed in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through
   `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`). A test
   asserts no editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through that
   module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
5. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
6. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` and the generated per-storyline
   docs/SVGs (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`); `npm run storylines:graph --
   --format json --check`, `npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and
   `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` pass. Edits that touch a
   hand-written documented row surface an explicit "manual documentation update
   required" result naming the doc-drift check. Covered by tests.
7. **Concurrency guard** — if `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load,
   the editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
8. **Game build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the
   production game bundle; verified by a build/test assertion (e.g. the editor
   entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts` graph).
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `src/README.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — the editor must reuse the existing transactional,
  self-validating author operations; it must not introduce a second way to edit
  `src/card-data.csv`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`vite-node`/Vitest/
  Playwright toolchain.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — the manifest/mmd generators must stay
  timestamp-free; the existing drift test must continue to pass.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Backward compatibility** — CSV schema/column order and legacy
  `hasChoices`/accept/reject semantics must be preserved; the C1 regression
  harness must stay green.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to
  players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — richer option semantics (conditional/cost-gated effects,
  `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) are out of scope; the editor edits today's two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Manifest + schema** — `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` (generated,
  deterministic, 5 storyline ids, 71 nodes, 15 edges, 1 cycle) and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` (draft-07, `additionalProperties:
  false`).
- **Graph export** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` with
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json` and a `--check` drift
  guard; committed `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`.
- **Transactional author API** — `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (CLI
  `npm run storylines:author`, `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`): builds the
  edited CSV in memory, loads it through the typed model and validates **before**
  writing; `--dry-run` and `--csv <path>` supported.
- **Validator** — `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (`validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`), cycles informational, `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in.
- **Model/seam** — `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (`compileStorylineFromEvent`,
  `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`, `resolveStorylineOption`,
  `pushChainCard`); CSV authoring keeps the two-way representation.
- **Stack** — Vite + Phaser + Electron; scripts run under `vite-node` because
  the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query.
- **Gap** — no interactive editor; the only graph view is the static generated
  Mermaid/JSON plus the per-storyline SVG pages rendered by
  `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`,
  completed in `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). Nothing can edit through a UI.
- **Reusable pieces for the editor** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` exports
  `filterManifestByStoryline`, `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`,
  `describeEventImpact` and `describeChoiceRouting` (per-storyline grouping and
  labels); `src/CsvChecksum.ts` exports `computeCsvChecksum` (CSV change
  detection, already used for card-art regeneration); `validate-storylines.ts`
  exports `formatStorylineReport` / `storylineReportToJson` (report rendering).
  The committed manifest currently holds 5 storylines, 71 nodes, 15 edges and
  1 cycle.

## Desired change

1. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   modules.
2. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
3. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.

# Add cost-based affordability filtering to the draw-time option snapshot

## Summary

`createPendingStorylineChoice(event, state)` already freezes a
condition-filtered option list into `PendingEventChoice.options`. Extend that
draw-time filter so options whose declarative `cost` exceeds the player's
coins/reputation are omitted from the snapshot. No new state field is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost filter.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `state.resourceBank.coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `state.resourceBank.reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; options with no cost are always included.
- **Combined filtering.** An option must pass both the existing `condition` callback and the new cost check to be presented; unaffordable options are omitted rather than disabled.
- **Snapshot stability.** Filtering happens once at draw time and the frozen `pending.options` list is what resolution reads; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before, and legacy pending choices without a snapshot still fall back to recompiling.
- **Boundary coverage.** Cost equal to the current balance is affordable; both coins and reputation gates are enforced when both are specified.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — cost filtering inside `compileStorylineFromEvent` / `createPendingStorylineChoice`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — document that the existing `options` snapshot carries cost-filtered lists.

## Deliverables

- Cost-aware draw-time filtering.
- Unit tests for omission, boundary equality, and combined coins/reputation gates.

# Resolve declarative conditional successors at option resolution

## Summary

Evaluate an option's ordered `conditionalSuccessors` rules at resolution time
inside `resolveStorylineOption`, ahead of the existing random candidate draw.
Rules are declarative and serialisable; the callback `successorResolver` keeps
highest precedence as the existing escape hatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule matching `state.resourceBank` field determines the pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback when no conditions match.
- **Precedence.** `successorResolver` (callback) wins when present; otherwise conditional rules run before `successorIds` (random draw) and the legacy single `successorId`, and a matching rule consumes no RNG draw.
- **Null target.** A matching rule with `successorId: null` ends the chain without pushing a card.
- **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match fallback; matched successor pushed via `pushChainCard`.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` keep today's resolver/random/single-successor behaviour.

"As a content designer, I want an edit to be previewed and validated before it

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — thin bridge over the existing modules,

  - `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — `validateStorylines`,
